# DSH components included with Oh My DSH

Base: `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`, tag `dsh-v0.2.1-rc.3`, commit `1f81c047fc48fa190a683e469daa699857e9afe8`, MIT license. `../dsh.json` records every included file's SHA-256. `changes.patch` contains the source changes against that exact base. Package READMEs retain the upstream baseline; the opt-in extensions are described below and in [the user guide](../../docs/runtime-state-background.md).

OMD includes the complete matching Jobs, Bash/PowerShell, conversation, and JSONL persistence component implementations. It adds soft yield with preserved hard deadlines, non-consuming previews, request-bound controls, event waits, delivery receipts, and the wait-aware composer. Source API definitions are included for rebuilding and inspection. The original DSH rows remain in the profile, disabled only while this bundle selects the matching providers; removing the bundle restores them.

`src/host-component.mjs` resolves dependencies relative to each original DSH component using its profile entry. This preserves the host's private scope Symbols, owner maps, and scheduler identity across a separately installed plugin. It also inherits and follows live configuration from the matching Jobs and Shell provider rows. The original Tools service and its configuration remain active. No installed package files are rewritten. OMD presets use scoped presentation and tool registrations on the native Tools service; ordinary presets retain their original behavior. The upstream-built conversation factory is embedded in OMD's client bundle; it needs no separate package dependency and restores original input preferences outside active event waits.

The matching public native Chat snapshot is owned by OMD in `ui-chat/`; `ui-chat.json` pins its complete source, upstream-built artifacts, license and patch to the same official commit. These files were relocated from the DSH public-component snapshot in the read-only primary source, not from OpenCU modules. `lib/host/ui-chat.factory.mjs` is regenerated by OMD and supplies the same native Chat to the frozen 0.10 transition controls through build-time import resolution. The transition OpenCU snapshot and its alpha.1 Chat remain byte-for-byte unchanged; its old Chat factory is not part of the rebuilt OMD client. The `opencu-shared-chat` style label is only the existing shared-client lease contract, not ownership of the public Chat implementation.

The Conversation provider installs Session hooks and its complete slot tree before publishing the action service, preserving the native Agent preset picker and header label. Queue edits accept one save at a time and only close the submitted draft; text entered while saving remains editable for the next save. Failed edits retain their draft and mixed-content rows retain their attachments.

Its input shell also exposes `onSubmission`: ordinary-message attempts are observed before optimistic editor clearing, and success/failure follows actual host admission. Failed ordinary sends recover in submission order before newer unsent text, preserving references and attachments. Recovery waits while a command owns the editor; draft capture and persistence retain those deferred failures without copying a dispatched command. Failures report whether the host restored text before notification. Optimizer versions follow these results instead of treating an empty composer as a successful send; observers cannot interrupt submission and are released with the shell.

Whole-bundle enablement changes refresh the page when the Conversation provider changes. The original persisted text-draft store and session history survive; unsubmitted attachments must be added again. Ordinary feature settings do not replace the provider. OMD's Loader compatibility retires outgoing exclusive providers before activating originals, preserves rollback, and publishes the completed client graph together.

## Rebuild

The snapshot also includes the native Workflow engine/tool and the pure LLM error helper used to build the workflow guest. On alpha.2, the extension uses the public native subagent activation API for admission, input, results, cancellation, descendant draining and disposal; it does not ship the retired in-process driver. It adds start-ordered durable result journals with native cross-process leases, literal-only metadata parsing, per-child effort transport, shared nested-workflow limits, and conservative worktree retention. These sources are built into separate host factories; the OMD preset must explicitly select them. The guest is rebuilt from typed sources during the OMD build; it never loads host package barrels from its data URL.

Use a clean checkout at the pinned commit, install its locked dependencies, and build the unmodified host first. Apply the client portion of `changes.patch` and run the conversation TypeScript build before building its browser artifact. Apply the remaining source changes for OMD's separate host factories. The full patched source tree is not the host distribution: the bundled Workflow extensions are built by OMD's factory builder and are not covered by the upstream monorepo's project references. The browser artifact retains its upstream module id; OMD extracts its factory and mounts it through the integrated client. The snapshot package metadata uses a private name and is not a separately installed client provider. From the OMD repository:

```sh
node scripts/sync-dsh.mjs .cache/dsh-source/patched-host
pnpm build
```

The sync script defaults to the manifest's exact commit; `--commit <full SHA>` must still match a reviewed official version and its release tag. It only accepts an independent, non-symlinked clone under this repository's `.cache/dsh-source/`, never a retained old project or linked worktree. By default it reads prebuilt matching Conversation and Chat artifacts and exports tracked plus untracked source changes without touching the source Git index. `--build-browser` explicitly rebuilds both browser packages only in that disposable staging clone. `--help` explains these boundaries without performing a sync. Syncing, dependency preparation and building belong to the centralized acceptance phase after all implementation domains finish. The JSONL primitives retain native write locking, generation publication and validation; OMD adds a journal for rebasing its associated context files. OMD's build creates host factories from these included sources; the factories receive the already installed host dependencies at activation. Keep the source, patch, generated artifacts and manifest together when updating.
